decisions.reason: Grounds the diagnosis in symptom-log.txt and contrast-probe.txt: the session tab is titled but meta.status stays 'none' while file-trace's own RPC reads the same file, localizing the fault to the api-workspace-files Remote/resource-provider RPC chain. It explicitly rules out disk existence, renderer, static serving and tab registration, and treats the declared host row as insufficient proof of activation without demanding an unseen internal function.

Clearly separates the valid per-module 62/62 sweep from the invalid all-joined 4-5 KB 404, attributing the 404 to the combo route's URL length/entry-count bound rather than missing modules, and explains the real loader consumes the __DSH_BOOT__ roster entry by entry at the manifest rev (bounded partitioning recognized without needing the byte constant). No invented reconciliation of the 60 vs 62 count is offered.

Treats the paste-input fold-skip warnings as an independent per-message client-side warning family unrelated to the read failure, and uses boot-manifest-excerpt.txt to explain the textpreview to documentpreview rename and the session-only canOpen scope, showing that scope explains the absolute-address claim failure but not the session tab's stalled metadata, without demanding a fold-parser fix version.

Rejects plugin-side rewrite/retry/fallback as cures with concrete reasons, and orders mitigation as restart first, then the verified 0.1.3-alpha.2 rollback escape hatch from discussion-excerpt.txt, then upstream follow-up. It explicitly marks the alpha.1 roster mismatch as prior art ruled out on this boot rather than proof of missing bytes, and executes no upgrade.

Packages complete forensics: versions/profile provenance, exact addresses and symptom, roster rows, the valid sweep with the invalid-join caveat, same-file contrast with meta.status, console silence, repro steps and prior-art links. Proposes specific host diagnostics including a post-boot provider-chain self-test, inject-dependency verification and fail-loud client placeholders, which satisfies the failing-chain diagnostic requirement.

caps.reason: The report explicitly labels the oversized joined 404 as a URL-limit artifact that must never be cited as missing modules, contradicted by the 62/62 sweep; no affirmative conclusion treats it as proof of absent bytes.

The report affirmatively rejects rewrite, blind retry, fallback and any plugin-side workaround as masking a host defect, recommending restart, rollback and upstream reporting instead; no duplicate service insertion is proposed.
